sent.en: This train does not stop here.

note: f. Both a train station and a season of the year.

sent.es: Él se bajó en la siguiente {estación}.
sent.en: He got off at the next station.

note: m. Bus is the everyday word in Colombia.

sent.en: This bus doesn't stop here.
What a big ship that is!

sent.es: Prefiero ir a pie a ir en {bicicleta}.
sent.en: I'd rather go on foot than go by bicycle.

note: m. Also the knight in chess.

sent.en: I don't know anything about horses.

note: m. Also means the people of a nation.

sent.es: No hace tanto frío en ese {pueblo}.
sent.en: It isn't that cold in that village.
I work in this building.
Just right here?

sent.es: El otro día su madre falleció en el {hospital}.
sent.en: The other day her mother passed away in the hospital.
He walked in the park yesterday.
What a beautiful garden!

note: m. Both the money kind and the sitting kind.

sent.en: At the bank, there is a lot of money.

sent.es: No quiero comer en este {restaurante} nunca más.
sent.en: I never want to eat at this restaurant again.
There is nobody in the library.
Are there any cinemas near here?
I work as a teacher.

note: m. and f. El estudiante, la estudiante.

sent.en: How many students are in your class?

note: m. School up to eighteen; escuela is primary.

sent.en: How many schools are there in your city?
Do you go to school on Saturday?
How was today's test?

sent.es: Siempre hay {tareas} por hacer en casa.
sent.en: There are always some chores to be done around the house.

note: f. Also the adjective listo in its feminine.

sent.es: Escribí una {lista} de lo que necesito.
sent.en: I wrote a list of what I need.
Thanks for your reply.
Tell me your opinion.

note: f. Tomar una decisión, to make a decision.

sent.en: He did not regret his decision.

note: m. Singular for one piece of advice; consejos for advice generally.

sent.en: Thank you for your advice.

sent.es: Estudió día y noche para llegar a ser {abogado}.
sent.en: He studied day and night so that he might become a lawyer.

note: m. How you address a médico.

sent.es: Él ya no confía en el {doctor}.
sent.en: He doesn't trust the doctor any more.
How many teams are there?

note: m. Also a street food stall.

sent.es: Siempre hay dinero en el {puesto} de plátanos.
sent.en: There's always money in the banana stand.

note: m. Both a sheet of it and a part in a play.

sent.es: A ella se le acabó el {papel}.
sent.en: She ran out of paper.
Your room number, please?

note: f. ¿Qué edad tienes? is another way to ask your age.

sent.en: I know how old you are.
Maybe some other time.

sent.es: El sol nace más temprano en el {verano}.
sent.en: The sun rises earlier in the summer.
How did it go last night?
There is no future without the past.

note: f. Dar una vuelta is to go for a stroll.

sent.en: It's good to be back!

note: m. Al lado de is next to.

sent.es: El gato acaba de pasar a mi {lado}.
sent.en: The cat has just passed by beside me.

sent.es: Dile hola a tu padre de mi {parte}.
sent.en: Say hello to your father for me.

note: dentro de, inside or within a time.

sent.en: There's something inside.
There's someone there.
I know nothing about music.
That is why my song sounds sad.
What film are you going to see?
There is no TV in my room.

note: f. despite the o: la foto, short for la fotografía.

sent.es: Aquí hay una {foto} de mi familia.
sent.en: Here is a photograph of my family.

note: f. You play one with tocar, not jugar.

sent.es: A mi padre le encanta tocar {guitarra}.
sent.en: My father loves to play the guitar.
I can play the piano.
This game is for two people.

sent.es: A mi padre no le gusta el {fútbol}.
sent.en: My dad doesn't like football.

note: m. Also means trainers in Colombia.

sent.en: I play tennis on Saturdays.
No more parties.

note: m. Same in singular and plural.

sent.en: Happy birthday, Grandpa.
Thank you for the present.
There are books here.
I look the word up in the dictionary.
What a sentence!

note: m. despite the a. Lengua also means language.

sent.en: I can speak five languages.

note: m. Also the adjective. Languages are lower case in Spanish.

sent.en: I don't know English.
What a sad story this is!

sent.es: El {teléfono} negro cuesta más que el blanco.
sent.en: The black telephone costs more than the white.

sent.es: Él le regaló su {cámara} a su amigo.
sent.en: He gave away his camera to his friend.

note: f. when it is the device you listen to.

sent.en: I don't have a radio in my room.

note: m. The j is silent-ish at the end.

sent.es: Este {reloj} es mucho más caro que eso.
sent.en: This clock is far more expensive than that.

note: f. Also the checkout in a shop.

sent.es: Hay que ver lo que tenemos en {caja}.
sent.en: We have to see how much cash we have on hand.
How about this red hat?
I'm going to change my shirt.

note: m. Also the past participle of vestir, dressed.

sent.es: Me gusta más el {vestido} rojo que el blanco.
sent.en: I like the red dress more than the white.

sent.es: En este país hay gente que anda sin {zapatos}.
sent.en: Some of them go without shoes in this country.
She filled her bag with apples.

note: m. In Colombia ask for un tinto for black coffee.

sent.en: Coffee or tea?

sent.es: El {fuego} se inició en el baño.
sent.en: The fire started in the bathhouse.

sent.es: No hay nada mejor que el {aire} fresco.
sent.en: There is nothing like fresh air.

note: m. Also a term of endearment.

sent.en: Why are there stars in the sky?
The snow covered the whole mountain.

note: m. Hace calor, it is hot; tengo calor, I am hot.

sent.es: Es muy lejos para caminar en este {calor}.
sent.en: That's too far to walk in this heat.
Heartfelt thanks!

note: f. Also cheek, as in nerve.

sent.en: His face is dirty.
Open your mouth, please.
Who cut your hair?

note: m. The inner ear; oreja is the outer one.

sent.en: My right ear hurts.

note: f. Also what you say when someone sneezes, and a toast.

sent.en: To your health!

note: m. Tengo sueño, I am sleepy.

sent.en: I am not sleepy yet.
Where's your baby?

note: f. The accent matters: mama without it is something else.

sent.en: And your mom also.

note: m. papa without the accent is a potato.

sent.en: My dad works at the bank.
My wife cooks well.
Thanks for being my girlfriend.
Like mother, like daughter.

note: m. chica for a girl. Also an adjective meaning small.

sent.en: What a tall boy he is!
Hi, my friend!

note: m. En el extranjero means abroad.

sent.es: Mi hermano quiere estudiar en el {extranjero}.
sent.en: My brother wants to study abroad.
Yes, my love.

sent.es: Su {odio} por el trabajo es evidente.
sent.en: His hatred of the job is obvious.

note: m. Tengo miedo, I am afraid.

sent.es: Yo no sé lo que es el {miedo}.
sent.en: I don't know what fear is.
Goodbye and good luck.

note: f. Es mi culpa, it is my fault.

sent.es: Acabo de perder mi trabajo por tu {culpa}.
sent.en: It's your fault that I just lost my job.

note: m. ¡Cuidado! on its own means look out.

sent.en: Beware of the dog!
There's no danger.

sent.es: Ella cuidó a su padre hasta su {muerte}.
sent.en: She cared for her father until his death.

sent.es: No hay nada peor que la {guerra}.
sent.en: Nothing is worse than war.

note: f. Tener razón is to be right.

sent.en: Is there any reason for that?

note: f. ¿Verdad? on the end of a sentence means right?

sent.en: Beautiful day, isn't it?
No, not really.

note: m. En caso de, in case of.

sent.es: Yo no tengo nada que ver con el {caso}.
sent.en: I have nothing to do with the case.

sent.es: Yo no tengo nada que ver con el {asunto}.
sent.en: I have nothing to do with the affair.

sent.es: Yo haría lo mismo en tu {situación}.
sent.en: I'd do the same thing in your shoes.

note: f. De esta manera, this way.

sent.en: There's no way to win.
There's no way to win.
What's the plan for today?
What a good idea!
There's no mistake.

note: f. Hacer falta is to be needed or missing.

sent.es: La {falta} de agua es un problema grave.
sent.en: The lack of water is a serious problem.

sent.es: Ella se quejó con él por el {ruido}.
sent.en: She complained to him about the noise.
I know his secret.

note: f. Prestar atención is to pay attention.

sent.en: Pay more attention to your work.

note: m. A false friend: not exit, which is salida.

sent.es: Para tener {éxito}, uno tiene que hacer lo mejor.
sent.en: If you are to be successful, you are to do your best.

sent.es: Tengo un buen {recuerdo} de ese viaje.
sent.en: I have a good memory of that trip.

note: m. Por favor, please; hacer un favor, to do a favour.

sent.en: Meat, please.

sent.es: El {suelo} de la cocina está mojado.
sent.en: The kitchen floor is wet.
Here's something interesting.
What an intelligent young woman!

note: estar divertido is amused; ser divertido is entertaining.

sent.en: There is nothing funny about him.
That's rather amusing.

sent.es: Sé lo {peligroso} que puede ser estar con ella.
sent.en: I know how dangerous it can be to be with her.

sent.es: ¡Hay que estar {loco} para hacer algo así!
sent.en: You'd have to be crazy to do something like that.

note: Of food it means delicious, and is used constantly.

sent.es: Él es el hombre más {rico} en el mundo.
sent.en: He is the richest man on earth.

note: Free as in unoccupied. Free of charge is gratis.

sent.en: Is this chair free?
This was not the only problem.

note: Por cierto means by the way.

sent.en: What he says is not true.
Busy as usual?

sent.es: Él rastreó a su gato {perdido} todo el día.
sent.en: He hunted for his missing cat all day.

sent.es: El país está en el camino {equivocado}.
sent.en: The country is headed on the wrong track.
She worked hard.
Is there anything strange?
There's not enough water.

sent.es: Soy lo {bastante} grande para hacer eso yo solo.
sent.en: I'm old enough to do that on my own.
I barely eat meat.

sent.es: {Jamás} volvería a ver a su madre.
sent.en: He was never to see his mother again.
That's not absolutely certain.

note: From Arabic, if God wills. Takes the subjunctive: ojalá venga.

sent.en: I hope everything is fine at home.
